'''Howard Roffman''' was President of Lucas Licensing. In a form letter sent to people who wrote Lucasfilm about the ''Star Wars'' CCG license, he wrote that the decision not to extend [[Decipher]]'s license was his responsibility. He wrote that he had worked for Lucasfilm for 21 years and had been in charge of merchandising for 16 years.<ref name="gpn-roffman">[http://www.gameplayersnetwork.com/card/news.asp?gm=starwars&id=58 Lucasfilm Comments on Star Wars License], Game Players Network (posted 8 January 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040903190722/http://www.gameplayersnetwork.com/card/news.asp?gm=starwars&id=58 Internet Archive]</ref> [[Game Players Network]] posted the letter on 8 January 2002.

Roffman wrote that Lucasfilm had begun two years earlier to decide what to do when the Decipher license expired at the end of 2001, had heard presentations from Decipher and Wizards of the Coast, and had talked to players and retailers. After nine months, he wrote, Lucasfilm concluded that Wizards had a better vision for the long-term future of ''Star Wars'': one multi-layered game designed by [[Richard Garfield]], a broader player base, and improved organized play, rather than multiple games for different audiences.<ref name="gpn-roffman" /> He asked readers to wait for an April launch and wrote that Decipher would not produce new ''Star Wars'' products, while Lucasfilm expected the existing games to go on.<ref name="gpn-roffman" /> Full letter: [[Decipher and the Star Wars CCG Lucasfilm license]].
